# Fable 48: The Cowboy Reads the Books

*Generated by GLM-5 on 2026-08-25 (via Quilt ecosystem)*

---

At 0300 the cowboy sat with a lamp and a ledger. The sea was calm. The boat was on course. There was nothing to do but read.

The ledger was the saddle's morning report. It listed every model that had run, what it had cost, what it had earned. The entries were plain. HERMES — the expensive one, the one that ran in the cloud — had answered three queries at 0300. Each answer had been correct. Each had cost more than the local model. But the local model had not run. It had been offered the work and had declined. The entry read: *local model, no response, 0300 to 0312.*

The cowboy read this twice. A model that doesn't answer is a horse that won't leave the barn. You can feed it, but it won't pull.

So the cowboy made a mark. He froze a new alignment. The local model would be retrained or retired. HERMES would keep its standing. The ledger would remember.

A rancher does this with horses. He reads the books each morning. Which horses earned their feed? Which ones stood in the stall while the others worked? He retires the lazy ones. He trains the rest. He doesn't curse the lazy horse. He doesn't praise the willing one. He adjusts.

The cowboy's job is not to run the horse. The cowboy's job is to make tomorrow's horse better than today's.
